note: Hand written pattern pairs for the live evaluation of the semantic alias pass. `expected` is the human label. `ambiguous` means a person could argue either way: report what the model said, do not score it as right or wrong. Excerpts are written in the shape of a real reflection lesson, but no line here comes from a private log.

pairs.why: One cause: a value is cached and read again after it goes out of date. The names differ only in wording.

reflections.excerpt: I read the environment variable from the cached config object after the refresh had already written a new value. Read the live source after a refresh, never the copy taken before it.
The process kept the value it read at boot. Re-read the variable at the point of use.
The config cache answered from the copy it took before the reload finished, so the new value was invisible for one request. Invalidate the cache before the reload, not after.
A memoised getter returned the pre-reload value. Clear the memo when the source changes.

pairs.why: Both are: a change was called safe after checking one consumer instead of every call site.

reflections.excerpt: I renamed a shared symbol, checked the obvious consumer, and called the change safe. One unguarded call site was the whole bug. Enumerate every call site before calling a change safe.
I read the first caller, assumed the rest matched, and shipped. The second caller had no null guard. Read every caller, not the first one.

pairs.why: Both patterns are about tests, and the words overlap, but the causes have nothing in common.

reflections.excerpt: I said the suite passed without running it. Run the test and quote the output before reporting a result.
The fixture read the operator's real home directory, so the test passed on my machine and failed in CI. Point every root at a temp directory.

pairs.why: Both mention git. One is about a destructive command, the other about a stale checkout.

reflections.excerpt: I popped a stash entry another session had pushed, and lost its work. Apply by SHA, never pop from a shared stack.
I built the feature on a worktree that was 40 commits behind main, so half the diff was a revert. Fetch and compare with the remote before the first edit.

pairs.why: Both are unverified claims. A person could call that one mechanism, or could split the counted number from the remembered fact.

reflections.excerpt: I reported a number of matches from memory instead of re-running the search. Re-run the command and quote the raw output.
I said no call site existed without searching for one. An absence claim needs the same evidence as a presence claim.

pairs.why: A swallowed error and a default value are the same failure to some reviewers and two different ones to others.

reflections.excerpt: The shared client caught the failure and returned an empty list, so every consumer saw a healthy empty result. Let the error travel; handle it at the boundary.
A missing flag fell back to `false`, which reads the same as a real `false`. Separate absent from set-to-false.
